name: Tabular Transformation Discovery Harness
description: Reverse engineering the latent data-generating mechanisms of synthetic and legacy tabular datasets is a fundamental inverse problem for evaluating program comprehension, automated feature engineering, and inductive reasoning in artificial intelligence. While Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate remarkable competence in forward mathematical reasoning and code generation, their ability to infer, isolate, and reconstruct complex transformation chains from input-output tabular observations remains underexplored. In this paper, we introduce the Tabular Transformation Discovery Harness, an autonomous, two-tier evaluation framework designed to benchmark LLMs on inverse tabular reasoning across six standardized syntactic complexity levels (Level 0 to Level 5). The harness separates an agentic discovery phase in an iterative, tool-assisted sandbox from a strictly isolated, black-box functional evaluation on hidden test distributions, governed by an adaptive tiered budget controller. We evaluate LLM agents (OpenAI GPT-5-mini and GPT-5-nano) against deterministic baselines across 144 benchmark tasks. Our empirical results show that while LLM agents achieve high functional accuracy on atomic transformations (1.0000 for mini, 0.8750 for nano at Level 0), performance progressively declines on deep compositions (0.5000 and 0.3889 at Level 2) and complex hybrid interaction graphs (0.1181 and 0.0069 at Level 5) primarily due to search space explosion and tool budget exhaustion.
